free_tier.stated: 100 GB relay egress per month, 10,000 concurrent connections, 5 MB/s rate

egress.terms: metered at 100 GB/month, which is 3.3 GB/day

chaining: the paid fallback for the 7-10% of iroh connections that fail to hole-punch; it composes with the transport and not with a free budget.

identity_cost.detail: an n0 account and an API key

reliability_note: the allowance is a 30-day trial rather than a persistent free tier

evidence.proved: up to 10,000 concurrent connections, 100 GB relay egress per month then USD 0.09/GB, a 5 MB/s rate limit, and a 30-day trial on Pro

notes: The free public relays are a separate product with deliberately unpublished limits.

extras.transit_note: the paid relay transits bytes, which is why it meters them at 100 GB per month

interface_detail: an iroh relay URL attached to a project, spoken over QUIC
binding_note: the monthly byte allowance in egress.free_allowance is what runs out, and no kind in the six-value vocabulary names a byte volume over a period counted per account. per-ip-shaping is the closest, because it is the only kind that bounds a volume, and its subject here is the account rather than the caller's address
limits_note: the allowance is a byte volume over a period, which none of the six kinds names; the number is in egress.free_allowance and binding names per-ip-shaping as the nearest kind
